title: Shape Your Data
goal: Structs name a shape with fields; enums name the alternatives; match handles them.

sections.text: A struct names a shape: fields with types. You build one by filling in every field - Rust has no partially built values (E0063 if you forget one).

sections.code:
struct User { name: String }

let u = User { name: String::from("Ferris") };
sections.caption: Every field named, every field filled.

sections.text: Behavior lives in an `impl` block. A method that only reads takes `&self`; a method that consumes its value takes `self`. The difference is not style: after a `self` method runs, the value is gone, and a second call is E0382. You will feel this in the puzzle.
An enum is the other shape tool: a value that is exactly one of a fixed set of variants, each optionally carrying data. `enum Command { Add(i32), Reset }` - two shapes, one type.

sections.caption: match takes each shape apart by name.

sections.text: `match` must cover every variant - the compiler counts (E0004). When you add a variant next month, every match you forgot becomes a compile error instead of a 3 a.m. bug. This exhaustiveness is one of Rust's best gifts; the Pattern Matching deck in Core goes deep on it.

explanation: Structs name a shape with fields; enums name the alternatives; match handles them.
